_comment: Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/AcidParting/tools/make_shape.py. Native frame, block units, controller cell at [0,0,0]: the front cell at ground level, where the fire door and the ash mouth are. One porcelain vessel in a sand bath over a small fire, under a brick hood open in front; vessels stand side by side in a row along x (up to parting.rowMax), sharing one chimney on one member's outlet, the others capped. No power and no forced air: natural draught, in at the ash mouth (ash, ashSide) under the damper, the fuel in at the fire door (firedoor, firedoorSide). depth is the fire door: 0 open, slid up in its guides (the rest pose), 1 shut. theta is the stoker's clock, carried by a ratio-0 rotate on the door: nothing turns. requires: the build's stages, brickwork (with the hoodiron part), lining and fittings (the bath, vessel and door parts) (build; the frame, iron, has none); the water line, pipecopper or pipelead (one straight ppex pipe with its brass cock), and the cock's key, cockshut or cockopen; the damper's place, damperopen, damperhalf or dampershut (one at a time); the fire, fuel (laid) or fire (burning); the vessel's contents: charge (granulated dore), acid, solution (the silver dissolved), gold (the parted gold), wash (the wash water); and outletcap. The brickwork's texture is the brick type's (bricks). vesselCell, vesselFace: the hood's cell, the vessel worked through its open front (vessel: its mouth); waterCell, waterFace: the top of the front row, where the player's ppex pipe meets the water line (cock: the nozzle's tip, where the water runs out); outletCell: the stack's head, in the back row, the chimney stood on its top; chimney: the shortest chimney, counted from the outlet up. See AcidParting/README.md.

build._comment: The build's stages, in order (a proposal for the owner but for the counts measured from the model). frame: the iron frame's grid recipe (with a hammer); placing it puts down the controller and its ghosts, and draws the frame part. Each stage then fits its requires when its materials are all in: brickwork (its alsoParts, the hood's lintel, comes with it at no cost of its own), then lining, then fittings (its parts: the sand bath with its sand, the vessel and the fire door; also: the damper, in one of its places). volumeBlocks: the stage's brick measured from the model, in blocks; its quantities are that at 2 fired bricks or 4 refractory bricks a block (the game's brick block recipes), rounded up, fire clay one per 2.5 refractory bricks. perClick stack: a click puts in as many of the held stack as are still needed. oneType: the first fired brick put in sets the brick type (bricks), and the rest must match. The parting vessel's own item is open (the game has no porcelain vessel). waterLine: one ppex straight pipe, copper or lead, fits the part of its metal, and a brass plate the cock, in one of its places (also). outletCap: an item interaction, not a stage.

bricks._comment: The fired brick types the brickwork takes (every game:burnedbrick type), each with the block its bricks make and that block's texture: the renderer sets the shape's 'brick' code to the vessel's type's base, with its overlays drawn over it (the crucible furnace's table). The type is the first brick put in; until then no brick is drawn.

parting._comment: minChimney: chimney blocks stood on the outlet, counted from it up (the crucible furnace's MinChimneyHeight); rowMax, rowAxis: vessels in a row, side by side along x, sharing one chimney; pipeMetals: the water line's metals, the part pipe<metal> drawn for the fitted one.
